description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/kvhslice.t's
inline `ok(1,"SKIP")` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING.  Not silent -- it dies
-- but it dies as an UNHANDLED CONDITION that takes the whole program down.

REPRO (scratch/p32-kvslice-bareword.pl):

    my %h = (i => 'I', j => 'J');
    my @a = %h{i};            # <-- dies
    print "[@a]\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  [i I]
  PCL:          Unhandled simple-error: Undefined subroutine &main::i called

THE SIBLINGS ARE ALL CORRECT (same probe, all four agree with perl):
    $h{i}       -> I        plain element, bareword autoquoted
    @h{i}       -> I        value hash slice, bareword autoquoted
    %h{'i'}     -> i I      kv-slice, key QUOTED
    %h{i, j}    -> dies     kv-slice, barewords
so the autoquote rule simply was not applied to the `%h{...}` subscript.

This is the family MEMORY warns about: "Grep for the sibling copy before
fixing an autoquote/callable site -- it drifts into 2-3 copies."  The
kv-slice is the copy that was never updated.  Check the key/value ARRAY slice
`%a[...]` in the same pass.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/kvhslice.t 28 and 29 (`scalar %h{i}` / the
value), jointly with #1023 (their scalar-context half).  Restored s464ay and
held back as fix targets in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv.  The companion suite
has t/op/kvhslice.t and t/op/kvaslice.t as DIFF files (kvaslice 23/15).

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the file's rows were inline `ok(1,"SKIP")` blaming a
"wantarray regression" and "context propagation through string eval".  Both
diagnoses are wrong -- the two kv-slice list-context rows the file blamed on
the wantarray regression PASS today (probed), and the bareword crash has
nothing to do with context.

RULE-12 NOTE: a bareword that resolves to no sub inside a subscript should not
reach the runtime as a call at all; if it does, the die should be perl-shaped
and trappable rather than an unhandled condition that ends the process.

=== DONE (s473t1) ===

FIXED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage), Pl/PExpr.pm.

CAUSE: `_kv_slice_node` was a THIRD copy of the subscript path.  The lone-
bareword autoquote lives in `_parse_subscript_ix` (which itself exists because
the interpolation path and the expression path had drifted into two copies of
the Word case), and the five kv-slice call sites went through
`_kv_slice_node`, which called `$self->parse(\@ix)` directly.  So no kv-slice
spelling ever got the autoquote -- exactly the sibling-copy family MEMORY
warns about.

FIX: `_kv_slice_node` calls `_parse_subscript_ix(\@ix, $type eq
'kv_slice_a_acc' ? 1 : 0)`.  The access kind is already in $type, which is
what `is_arr_braces` computed at each call site, so nothing new is derived.
The perl rule is POSITIONAL and sigil-blind: a HASH subscript always
autoquotes a lone bareword (even when a sub of that name exists), an ARRAY
subscript evaluates it when it is a known callable -- probed both ways, PCL
now matches.

ALL NINE SPELLINGS probed identical to perl 5.40.3 (they all died before):
  %h{i}  %h{i,j}  %$hr{i}  %{$hr}{i}  $hr->%{i}  delete %h{j}
  %a[1]  %a[k] with `sub k {2}`  %h{k} with `sub k {2}`

MEASURED: perl-tests/kvhslice.t PARTIAL 19+4/39 (38 produced) -> OK 21+3/39.
The two rows the registry comment held back as fix targets (28/29, now 29/30)
PASS.  Row 11 `correct value` -- an assertion inside `eval '... %h{i} ...'`
that never ran because the eval died -- now runs and fails honestly on task
#1023 (kv-slice in scalar context yields the COUNT, not the last VALUE).
cl/skip-registry.lisp's number-keyed entry moved 21 -> 22 (the file has two
rows described "correct hash"; its own stale detector said so).

corpus-diff over 111 perl-tests files: kvhslice.t IDENTICAL -- the bareword
spelling only occurs inside a string eval there, so the file's own emission
does not move.

GUARD: Pl/t/kvaslice-01.t rows 14-16 (13 -> 16), inverse-verified on a
`git archive 31473881` extraction (all three FAIL there).
subject: CRASH: a BAREWORD key inside a key/value hash slice `%h{i}` is not autoquoted -- PCL calls it as a sub and dies "Undefined subroutine &main::i"; `$h{i}`, `@h{i}` and the quoted `%h{'i'}` are all correct, so only the kv-slice subscript misses the autoquote
